desc: Implement direct marginal-threshold binary search with k_i = (x+P_i)//(2P_i), early break when F(x) > M, and answer = C(x) + (M - F(x))//(x+1); use exact integer arithmetic.
Derive O(N) count/sum formulas C(x) = sum floor((x+P_i)/(2P_i)) and F(x) = sum P_i*floor((x+P_i)/(2P_i))^2.
Handle edge cases: x = M (extra units = 0), T=0 when M < min P_i, duplicate P_i, N=1, huge P_i.
Validate against samples (output 3 and 53) and a brute-force check on small random cases; write only the answer to stdout.
Verified upper bound H = max_p p*(2s+1), s=isqrt(M//p), guarantees F(H) > M, giving ~47 binary search steps.
Confirmed correctness of the extra term via congruence argument: x maximal with F(x)<=M implies x+1 is the smallest affordable marginal, so each extra unit costs exactly x+1.
